topics.title: Coursework
topics.summary: KTH student guidance says the teacher’s course-specific rule takes precedence. Four common approaches describe possible course policies, not permission for every assignment.
topics.scope: Course-specific instructions control graded work. Staff/template/legal guidance is scoped reference material with incomplete current-source verification; institutional AI services do not authorize assessment use.

claims.text: KTH tells students that generative AI use in graded assignments and exams should follow the course-specific information, and that the teacher's course rule takes precedence over general guidance.

evidence.quote: First and foremost, you must follow your courses' course-specific information about how generative AI may be used in graded assignments and on the exam. No information on this page takes precedence over what your teacher says applies.
evidence.title: Considerations for studying with generative AI

claims.text: KTH student guidance says course-specific generative AI information usually follows one of four approaches: no use, only specific assignments, allowed with guidelines, or free use.

evidence.quote: The information is usually based on one of four common approaches to the use of generative AI: No use of generative AI tools allowed; Only allowed in specific assignments; Allowed according to given guidelines; Free use of generative AI tools.
evidence.title: Course-specific information about generative AI
evidence.location: What is meant by course-specific information about generative AI?

topics.title: Disclosure
topics.summary: Teacher guidance asks staff to remind students to disclose help and sources honestly; templates address when AI use must be accounted for. Apply the relevant course’s actual requirements.
topics.scope: Course-specific instructions control graded work. Staff/template/legal guidance is scoped reference material with incomplete current-source verification; institutional AI services do not authorize assessment use.

claims.text: KTH teacher guidance tells staff to remind students that, in any assessment, students shall honestly disclose help received and sources used.

evidence.quote: The ethical guidelines in each course plan states: "In any assessment, every student shall honestly disclose any help received and sources used.". Remind your students of this and have an open discussion with them about generative AI and your specific course.
evidence.title: Prevent and discourage prohibited use of generative AI
evidence.location: Foster a culture that does not use generative AI to cheat

claims.text: KTH staff guidance says its course-specific AI templates remind students that they are fully responsible for submitted material, explain when AI use must be accounted for, and warn that unauthorised generative AI use may lead to disciplinary action.

evidence.quote: The templates include: a reminder to students that they are fully responsible for all materials they submit; where relevant, how the use of generative AI should be accounted for; information that the unauthorised use of generative AI may lead to disciplinary action.
evidence.title: KTH's templates for course-specific information on generative AI
evidence.location: The templates are available in Canvas

topics.title: Privacy and data
topics.summary: Staff guidance advises removing personal data, while legal guidance requires examining GDPR, storage, third-party and training conditions. Copilot guidance still excludes personal, sensitive or confidential material.
topics.scope: Course-specific instructions control graded work. Staff/template/legal guidance is scoped reference material with incomplete current-source verification; institutional AI services do not authorize assessment use.

claims.text: KTH teacher guidance says teachers should remove personal data from material given to generative AI tools and ask students to do the same.

evidence.quote: Remove all personal data from the material you provide to the generative AI tool and ask your students to do the same.
evidence.title: Considerations for using generative AI
evidence.location: Take GDPR and copyright into account

claims.text: KTH legal guidance advises clearing prompts of personal data and says use of generative AI with personal data requires verifying GDPR-related grounds, storage, third-party, and training-data questions.

evidence.quote: You are advised to clear prompts from personal data when using generative AI tools. It is difficult to delete personal data once it has ended up in the training data of the tool, which makes a preliminary purge the safest and easiest method to ensure proper handling of personal data.
evidence.title: Legal aspects of generative AI

claims.text: KTH Copilot Chat guidance says the service still may not be used to share personal data, sensitive material, or confidential material.

evidence.quote: It is not permitted to share personal data, sensitive or confidential material in this type of cloud service.
evidence.title: Microsoft Copilot Chat

additionalTopics.summary: Teachers are asked to consider how AI affects learning and write course-specific acceptable-use information. The excluded Faculty Council wording is not recast here as a binding university-wide mandate.
